source.title: Boundary and Defect CFT: Open Problems and Applications

accepted.question_text: Are there general principles that determine which renormalization-group domain wall or conformal boundary state is selected from the set of possible interfaces or boundary states connecting the ultraviolet and infrared endpoints of a renormalization-group flow in boundary or defect conformal field theory?

evidence.quote: Are there general principles that select the RG domain wall(s)/boundary state(s) from the possible set connecting the UV and IR endpoints of RG flows?

accepted.question_text: What additional non-perturbative information about boundary and defect conformal field theories can supersymmetry provide, including through techniques such as supersymmetric localization?

evidence.quote: What more can SUSY tell us about bCFTs and dCFTs, for example via SUSY localization?

accepted.question_text: Do there exist monotonicity theorems for boundaries or defects in dimensions higher than two that generalize the two-dimensional g-theorem for boundary conformal field theories?

evidence.quote: Are there boundary or defect ‘c-theorems’ generalizing the g-theorem [208,209] of two-dimensional bCFT to higher dimensions?

accepted.question_text: To what extent can supersymmetry, the conformal bootstrap, integrability, topological field theory, and related boundary/defect conformal-field-theory techniques be turned into effective tools for answering open questions about renormalization-group domain walls, non-perturbative bCFT/dCFT data, higher-dimensional boundary or defect monotonicity theorems, and the discovery or classification of conformal boundary conditions and defects?

evidence.quote: To what extent can SUSY, the conformal bootstrap, integrability, topological field theory, and the other techniques discussed in these proceedings be used to address such questions?

accepted.question_text: Can supersymmetry, the conformal bootstrap, integrability, topological field theory, or related boundary/defect conformal-field-theory techniques lead to the discovery of new conformal boundary conditions, new defects, or entirely new perspectives on what quantum field theory is?

evidence.quote: Could they also lead to the discovery of new conformal boundary conditions, defects, or even entirely new perspectives on what QFT is?

accepted.question_text: How do double-trace interfaces in boundary or defect conformal field theory fuse with one another?

evidence.quote: our aim for the near future is to investigate the fusion process of the presented double trace interfaces by these methods.

accepted.question_text: Is there a higher-dimensional analogue of boundary-conformal-field-theory approaches to diagnosing and characterizing topological phases of matter, especially in settings where the relevant surface theories of (3+1)-dimensional symmetry-protected topological phases may be gapless or may carry topological order?

evidence.quote: It would be interesting to explore if there is a higher dimensional analogue of the approaches discussed in this article.

accepted.question_text: What are the explicit correction terms, beyond the leading linear-in-temperature contribution, to the low-temperature specific heat of the side-coupled quantum-dot model in an interacting Luttinger-liquid environment, and do their exponents indeed match the exponents inferred earlier from the renormalization-group analysis of the dot occupation?

evidence.quote: The corrections are still to be calculated but the exponents are expected to agree with those found earlier.

accepted.question_text: What dynamical mechanism is responsible for the complicated, almost fractal structures in the phase diagram of late-time boundary scattering outcomes for the sine-Gordon model with non-integrable Robin boundary conditions?

evidence.quote: what’s going on? What is the reason for the complicated, almost fractal, structures present in some parts of figure 6?

accepted.question_text: Can one develop a more effective collective-coordinate description of sine-Gordon scattering off a non-integrable boundary, despite the fact that the boundary interaction excites many additional modes?

evidence.quote: To this end, it would be nice to develop a more effective collective-coordinate description of the boundary situation.

accepted.question_text: Can the residual or asymptotic integrability of the sine-Gordon problem on the quarter-plane be exploited more deeply, for example through methods such as the Fokas approach, to analyze boundary-induced breaking of integrability?

evidence.quote: It is possible that more can be done to exploit integrability in the quarter-plane {(x, t) : x < 0, t > 0} which is the domain of our initial-value problem. The so-called Fokas method (see [79] for a recent review) is one possible avenue for further progress in this regard.

accepted.question_text: What is the correct quantum-field-theoretic description of the sine-Gordon model with a non-integrable boundary, and can techniques from quantum integrability still be adapted to study how integrability breaks down in that setting?

evidence.quote: Finally, at the back of our minds throughout this work was the thought to look at the corresponding quantum field theory.

accepted.question_text: Can extended chiral or superconformal algebras be used systematically to construct new non-topological, non-factorizing conformal defects in tricritical Ising theory and related models?

evidence.quote: We would like to look further into the use of extended algebras to construct new conformal defects.

accepted.question_text: Can the relevant boundary conditions for the free fermion and for the super-Virasoro minimal model SVIR3 be derived directly from first principles, or alternatively by adapting the methods of Novak and Runkel?

evidence.quote: It would be interesting to derive the boundary conditions for the free fermion and SVIR3 from first principles or using the methods of Novak and Runkel [84].

accepted.question_text: How can one- and two-point functions in defect conformal field theory be exploited more fully as input to the boundary conformal bootstrap, and what additional structure of the three-dimensional theory living on the defect must be understood in order to make that program work for the present AdS/dCFT system?

evidence.quote: The idea of using one- and two-point functions as input for the boundary conformal bootstrap equations is only in its infancy. Taking it further would potentially be very interesting but in order to fully exploit it for the present dCFT a better understanding of the 3D theory living on the defect is needed.

accepted.question_text: For the SO(5)-symmetric D3-D7-brane defect conformal field theory, can one find a closed tree-level formula for one-point functions when the full scalar SO(6) sector is considered, beyond the already understood chiral-primary case?

evidence.quote: As regards the integrability properties of one-point functions an interesting question is whether a closed formula can be found even at tree-level for the closely related SO(5) symmetric D3-D7-brane based dCFT.

accepted.question_text: Can one perform a genuine string-theoretic computation of the one-point function of a non-protected operator in the defect AdS/CFT setup?

evidence.quote: Finally, an open problem is to perform a string theoretical computation of the one-point function of a non-protected operator.

accepted.question_text: How should one incorporate finite-string-tension corrections, i.e. 1/λ corrections, into the large-N, large-'t Hooft-coupling analysis of four-point correlators in AdS5 × S5 supergravity?

evidence.quote: It would be interesting to discuss 1/λ corrections.

accepted.question_text: How can the analytic-bootstrap approach used for loop corrections in AdS5 × S5 be combined either with direct one-loop Witten-diagram computations or with integrability-based methods, so that the different approaches constrain and check one another?

evidence.quote: Other interesting directions would be to combine the method presented in this note with recent direct computations of Witten diagrams at one loop [150] and with integrability based approaches [151].

accepted.question_text: Can the bootstrap analysis of conformal field theories on real projective space be extended to holographic or otherwise strongly coupled theories such as N = 4 super Yang-Mills theory or Liouville theory, and if so does it agree with the corresponding holographic predictions?

evidence.quote: In the future, it would be interesting to study holographic models such as N = 4 super Yang-Mills theory or Liouville theory and compare them with the holographic predictions.

accepted.question_text: What is the correct analogue of complex analysis on quasi Riemann surfaces, and how can one develop it in parallel with ordinary complex analysis on genuine Riemann surfaces?

evidence.quote: Complex analysis on quasi Riemann surfaces needs to be developed in analogy with ordinary Riemann surfaces.

accepted.question_text: Is every quasi Riemann surface Q isomorphic to the space D_int_0(Σ) of integral 0-currents on some ordinary two-dimensional conformal space Σ with the same Jacobian, and if so how can that isomorphism be constructed concretely?

evidence.quote: Conjecturally, every quasi Riemann surface Q is isomorphic to D_int_0(Σ) for Σ the 2d conformal space with the same Jacobian as Q, the Jacobian being the complex torus made from the homology in the middle dimension.

accepted.question_text: Can one construct explicit families of local quasi-holomorphic curves from the complex disk into a quasi Riemann surface, for example when the ambient 2n-dimensional space is the sphere S^{2n}, so that local conformal-field-theoretic structure can be studied there?

evidence.quote: Explicit constructions of local quasi holomorphic curves are needed, say for M = S^2n.

accepted.question_text: What is the spacetime interpretation of the local gauge symmetry that appears in the bundle of quasi Riemann surfaces, such as the local SU(2)×SU(2) symmetry associated with the self-dual point of the two-dimensional Gaussian model?

evidence.quote: The local gauge symmetry in the bundle of quasi Riemann surfaces needs a space-time interpretation.

accepted.question_text: Can standard two-dimensional conformal-field-theory constructions, such as orbifolding and perturbation theory, be reproduced or generalized on quasi Riemann surfaces so as to generate new theories of higher-dimensional defects?

evidence.quote: It should be possible to imitate on the quasi Riemann surfaces the usual constructions of 2d cft such as orbifolding and perturbation theory.

accepted.question_text: When fields Φ(ξ) on quasi Riemann surfaces are restricted to very small defects ξ that look pointlike inside the ambient 2n-dimensional manifold, do the resulting ordinary local quantum fields define genuinely new local quantum field theories in 2n dimensions?

evidence.quote: Tiny defects look like points in M, so fields Φ(ξ) when restricted to the small ξ in Q will give ordinary local quantum fields on M. Will these form new local qfts in 2n-dimensions?
